title: Add telemetry slab with token-credit shadowing and ephemeral span heatmap
author: Maya Chen
description:
Background: We need a lower-noise, incremental aggregation layer that can produce short-lived (ephemeral) span heatmaps and surface 'shadowed' token credits to help SRE and finance teams reason about observed vs billed token consumption. Motivation: existing token-cost rollups inflate noise for short bursts and make it hard to see transient backpressure events. This PR introduces a lightweight 'telemetry slab' that creates compact differential rollups at invocation and span granularity and a metric we call token-credit-shadowed which estimates the delta between observed token production and chargeable token credits after routing/fallbacks/trim.

What this change does (single continuous description): Adds a telemetry slab collector and an incremental rollup writer; introduces two new metrics: "redwood.telemetry.slab.invocation_heatmap" (heatmap of span durations bucketed by token-phase) and "redwood.token.credit.shadowed" (gauge + rate that captures estimated shadowed credits per-tenant). Adds a dashboard (dashboards/telemetry-slab.json) with an ephemeral span heatmap panel and a token-credit delta explorer. Adds alert rules to reduce pager noise by auto-squashing long-tail deltas (ops/alerts/token-credit-shadowing.rules). Implements a feature flag (telemetry.slab.enabled) and a staged canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> global) with rollback hooks on elevated delta rate. Includes unit and simulation tests that validate slab accuracy under bursty workloads.

Checklist:
- [x] Collector and schema (telemetry/slab/collector.go, telemetry/schemas/token_credit.proto)
- [x] Incremental rollup writer and retention (pkg/telemetry/rollups)
- [x] Dashboard and saved queries (dashboards/telemetry-slab.json)
- [x] Alert rules and runbook snippets (ops/alerts/token-credit-shadowing.rules)
- [x] Feature-flag gated rollout and toggle in the console
- [x] Tests and a small synthetic replay bench (tests/telemetry/sim_slab_test.go)

Rollout plan: Start canary at 10% customers in us-east-1 for 48h, monitor redwood.token.credit.shadowed rate and slab reconciliation errors. If delta increases >20% for 2 consecutive windows, auto-roll back and open incident. After 72h stability at 10% we move to 50%, then global.

Operational notes: slab rollups are stored with a short TTL (48h) and a compacted archive job runs nightly to persist 7-day aggregates. The slab binary is CPU-light — profiling indicates <3% CPU of telemetry collector under our simulated 2x burst profile. The metric is exposed with tenant tags; no PII is emitted. There is a KMS check in the schema to ensure no raw prompt text is ever included.

Related: ENG-4821 (instrumentation spec), SUP-9123 (customer ticket that motivated delta explorer).

review_comments: Luca: Can we avoid emitting tenant identifiers in raw labels? Author: We only emit tenant_id as a hashed tag in high-card tables; the slab export uses an internal tenant_key and the dashboard joins on tenant_alias. Added extra KMS check to the serializer.

Priya: Alerting threshold seems aggressive for small tenants. Author: thresholds are shard-level and we added an adaptive multiplier based on tenant commit size; updated alert rule and added note in runbook.
Ethan: Add guardrail for slab memory under pathological invocations. Author: added a circuit that drops slab writes above 256MB mem and records a slab.drop metric; added unit tests.
ci_checks: perf-smoke: flaky on first run (OOM in synthetic), re-run passed
release_notes: Introduces telemetry slab: ephemeral span heatmaps and token-credit-shadowing metric. Adds dashboard and tuned alerts. Feature-flag gated; default off for existing customers. No breaking API changes.
notes: Privacy review completed: no prompt text exported. Finance/Cost team notified and will reconcile nightly archived aggregates with billing. Oncall playbook updated in docs/observability/token-credit-shadowing.md
